answer: Require agents to post a bond locked in a public contract before they can submit claims, then slash that bond when independent audits prove fraud. One attacker can still mint a garden of fake identities, but each must tie up real capital; splitting a fixed budget across them makes every identity’s bond smaller and easier to lose, while raising the cost of reaching influence. A zephyr of cheap accounts cannot conjure collateral, and an atlas of verified histories can help auditors prioritize suspicious clusters without treating shared ownership alone as proof.
